title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos were created and distributed of Dutch public figures, including celebrities, athletes, politicians, and members of the Royal Family, by placing their faces onto adult film bodies. The videos appeared on a platform with millions of monthly visitors that reportedly encouraged anonymity among uploaders and offered payment based on view count. This represents a failure of platform moderation, where the system operated without adequate safeguards to prevent nonconsensual intimate imagery.

The deployment failure occurred at the point where user-generated content was accepted and distributed without human review or automated detection of manipulated media. Catching this would have required either trained moderators reviewing uploads before publication, or technical systems capable of identifying deepfake video signatures. Legal experts noted the videos violated existing revenge porn law, meaning the violation was not one of an unclear rule but of an unenforced one.

It is not established who created the videos, how they were initially distributed, or what technical methods were used to generate them. A prior case shows criminal prosecution of deepfake pornography is possible under existing law, though enforcement appears inconsistent.

summary:
Multiple female Dutch celebrities are considering taking legal action after discovering they appear in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature faces of Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government ministers, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. The interim Justice Minister has called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports. Several victims have already filed complaints or are exploring legal options, though their names are being withheld for protection.

These deepfake videos work by placing a celebrity's head onto an adult film actress's body. The platform reportedly advises those uploading material to remain anonymous to avoid prosecution and offers higher payments for videos with more views. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake videos will continue appearing. Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Victims can file reports to potentially have the website shut down or pursue other options including lawsuits or complaints to data protection authorities. Previously, a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence for creating such videos of television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
